d: RigidConstraint connects two attachments with zero offset.
h:
A RigidConstraint connects two Attachments or Bones and ensures they stay in the same relative position/orientation to each other. This flexibility gives it additional functionality beyond WeldConstraint, such as attaching accessories to Attachments on a character rig.

To attach two BaseParts together, versus two Attachments or Bones, see WeldConstraint.

When creating a RigidConstraint using Studio's Constraint button, the tool behaves differently depending on whether you click on existing BaseParts, Attachments, or Bones after the tool is activated:

  • Clicking on an existing BasePart creates a new Attachment upon it as the intended RigidConstraint.Attachment0 or RigidConstraint.Attachment1.
  • Clicking on an existing Attachment or Bone uses that instance as the intended RigidConstraint.Attachment0 or RigidConstraint.Attachment1.

Following the second valid click, a new RigidConstraint is created to connect the two new attachments. If either the first or second click is not made on a BasePart, Attachment, or Bone, the workflow is canceled and no constraint is created.

kid.simple: A RigidConstraint locks two attachments (or bones) together so they stay in the same position and rotation relative to each other. It is like a weld, but it connects attachment points instead of whole parts. That makes it perfect for snapping a hat, backpack or tool onto a specific spot on a character, because characters already have attachments in useful places.
kid.analogy: It is like a snap button on a jacket: the two halves are fixed points, and when you snap them together they line up exactly.
keyPoints: RigidConstraint connects two Attachments or Bones, not two parts.
The two attachments are held at the same position and rotation relative to each other, with zero offset between them.
It can attach accessories to attachments on a character rig, which a WeldConstraint cannot do directly.
In Studio, clicking a part with the Rigid tool creates a new attachment on it; clicking an existing attachment or bone uses that one.
After two valid clicks, the constraint is created. If either click is not on a part, attachment or bone, nothing is created.
To glue two parts directly, use a WeldConstraint instead.

terms.attachment: A Roblox object you put inside a part to mark one exact point on it. Its Position is measured from the part's center, so an attachment at (0, 3, 0) sits 3 studs above the center of its part.
terms.bone: A joint inside an animated mesh. A constraint on a bone follows the bone as it animates.
terms.rig: The skeleton and joints of a character that let it move and animate.
terms.zero offset: No gap between the two attachment points. They are lined up exactly on top of each other, facing the same way.
terms.accessory: Something worn on a character, like a hat, hair or backpack.
terms.Massless: A part property. When true, the part adds no weight to the assembly, so a hat will not make the character lean or slow down.

example.title: Snap a glowing crown onto every player's head
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local function giveCrown(character)
	local head = character:WaitForChild("Head")
	-- R15 heads come with an attachment named HatAttachment on top
	local hatAttachment = head:WaitForChild("HatAttachment")

	local crown = Instance.new("Part")
	crown.Name = "Crown"
	crown.Size = Vector3.new(1.5, 0.5, 1.5)
	crown.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	crown.BrickColor = BrickColor.new("Bright yellow")
	crown.CanCollide = false
	crown.Massless = true   -- adds no weight to the character

	-- The crown's own attachment, 0.25 studs below its center (its bottom face)
	local crownAttachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
	crownAttachment.Position = Vector3.new(0, -0.25, 0)
	crownAttachment.Parent = crown

	local rigid = Instance.new("RigidConstraint")
	rigid.Attachment0 = hatAttachment
	rigid.Attachment1 = crownAttachment
	rigid.Parent = crown

	crown.Parent = character
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(giveCrown)
end)
explain: Every time a player's character spawns, `giveCrown` runs.
R15 character heads already have an attachment called HatAttachment at the top of the head. We wait for it to exist.
The crown is 0.5 studs tall, so its bottom face is 0.25 studs below its center. We put the crown's attachment there.
The RigidConstraint lines the two attachments up exactly, so the bottom of the crown sits on the HatAttachment spot and moves with the head.
`CanCollide = false` and `Massless = true` stop the crown from bumping into things or weighing the player down.

watchOut: Forgetting `Massless = true` on accessories can make characters tip or move strangely.
If the item appears in the wrong spot, check its attachment's Position. It is measured from the item's center.
Older R6 characters have different attachments than R15. Check the attachment name exists before using it.
RigidConstraint needs attachments or bones. If you just want to glue two parts, a WeldConstraint is simpler.
